# Architectural Design Exploration

## Concepts

An experiment compares design choices under controlled conditions. Fix workload, correctness criteria, tool environment, target technology, and measurement definitions before changing a configuration.

Latency, sustained throughput, timing slack, resource use, and area describe different aspects of a design. A smaller block can lose end-to-end performance through transfer overhead; a faster simulated datapath may miss its physical clock target.

## Implementation

Use a reusable subsystem as the experimental unit: processor/peripheral integration, a buffered stream, or a small accelerator. Store the specification, RTL, tests, formal properties, constraints, and implementation configuration together.

Separate FPGA and ASIC metrics. Keep technology, operating corner, clock period, software, and parameter values alongside each result. For power analysis, state the activity and modeling assumptions.

## Hands-on Experiments

Compare two buffer depths or hardware/software partitions. Change one variable per run, verify correctness, and then collect timing and resource results. Include failed configurations and explain why they failed.

Conclude with an integration package: interface contract, build commands, verification evidence, implementation summaries, and limitations. This follows a project progression from specification through verification, FPGA prototype, and ASIC implementation.
